audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[0..6].side read "Skill" on all seven rows while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Ahri, Skill, Ahri, Ahri, Ahri, Ahri, Skill.
audit.why: Five of seven rows disagreed. Ahri is at 55.63% over 2628 games and owns everything from level 3 to two items; only level 2 and the full-build row are genuinely even.

audit.whatIsWrong: The pull was attributed to his Q in four places ("E-root into Q-pull", "Bait his Q pull-in", "safe Q pull-in from max range"), and the root mechanic itself was described as a skillshot you dodge on the way out.
audit.why: Nevermove (E) does both jobs: Riot's text is a wave that travels forward, RETURNS to Swain, roots what it hits, and then Swain may recast to pull the rooted champions in. Death's Hand (Q) is a 750-range cone of piercing bolts with no displacement at all. Two consequences the page never gave the reader: the root lands on the RETURN pass, so sidestepping the outgoing wave is only half the dodge; and there is no separate cooldown to track for the pull — it is the same 12-second E.
audit.corrected: All four references rewritten onto Nevermove, with the return-pass root stated in spikes[0], whys[1], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.
sources: enemyKit E text, range and cd

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and spikes[1] both state that Demonic Ascension "roots him in place while draining HP", and wants.you[2] tells the reader to deny it by breaking line of sight.
audit.why: Riot's R text: Swain transforms and drains health from nearby enemies, and the form lasts indefinitely as long as he keeps draining champions. Nothing immobilises him — he walks at you the entire time — and the drain is a 650-radius effect, not a vision-dependent one, so line of sight breaks nothing. The real counterplay is the range number and the sustain condition: leave 650 and the form ends because there is no champion left to drain.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around the 650 radius, the 120-second cooldown and the drain-to-sustain condition.
sources: enemyKit R text, range and cd

audit.whatIsWrong: Vision of Empire never appears anywhere in the matchup, and Ravenous Flock's permanent max-health growth is only implied.
audit.why: Vision of Empire is a 22-second, 5500-to-7500-range eye that damages, slows, reveals and hands Swain a Soul Fragment off a champion hit — it is how he pressures a lane he is not standing in, and how he heals without touching you. Ravenous Flock turns those fragments into permanent maximum health, which is exactly why Grievous Wounds timing decides long trades.
audit.corrected: Added to breakdown.early, wants.foe[3] and ahead.

notes: Two mechanical errors that would change how a player behaves. (1) The pull was attributed to Death's Hand (Q) in four places — it is a recast of Nevermove (E), the same 12-second cooldown, so the reader was told to track a spell that has no displacement at all. Riot's E text also puts the root on the RETURN pass, which the matchup never mentioned; sidestepping the outgoing wave is only half the dodge and that alone explains a lot of lost trades. (2) 'Demonic Ascension roots him in place' is stated twice and is false — the form leaves him fully mobile, drains within 650, and persists only while a champion is inside it; the paired advice to 'break line of sight' does nothing, since the drain is radius-based. Both replaced with the range and the sustain condition. Vision of Empire (22s, 5500-7500 range, grants a Soul Fragment on a champion hit) appeared nowhere despite being how Swain heals and pressures without walking anywhere; it is now in three fields. Anti-heal advice in report[8] was already correct here and was left alone. Level chart disagreed on five of seven rows. Not asserted: whether Charm interrupts Demonic Ascension's transformation cast, and whether Nevermove's root is tenacity-reduced or cleansable.
